item.title: Assembly Drill 2026-11-11: crackme
item.description:
Target: Windows x86-64.
``` check: lea eax, [rcx+rdx] cmp eax, 100 jne fail mov eax, ecx sub eax, edx cmp eax, 20 jne fail mov eax, 1 ret fail: xor eax, eax ret ```
`check(int a, int b)` takes two arguments. Which `a` (ecx) and `b` (edx) make it return 1?
---
**Answer:** `a = 60`, `b = 40`
1. Windows x64 passes the first integer arg in `ecx` and the second in `edx`; `lea eax, [rcx+rdx]` adds them into a third register without touching either input or the flags. 2. The two checks give `a + b == 100` and `a - b == 20`; any mismatch jumps to `fail`, where `xor eax, eax` returns 0. 3. Adding the equations gives `2a = 120`, so `a = 60`, then `b = 100 - 60 = 40` (check: 60 - 40 = 20).
